text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed in thin trading, despite some signs of reawakening demand.

Bogota's IBB index drifted up 0.06 percent to 871.38 pesos on a 1.8 million peso volume while Medellin's IBOMED general price index dipped 0.04 percent to 13,625.95 on a trading volume of 758 million pesos.

"Prices are still flat and volume remained low but there is evidence of some demand. Existing shareholders don't want to give away shares, while potential buyers want prices to rise overnight so they can make a quick profit," a Bogota broker said."

Main movers on the Bogota exchange included the Banco de Bogota, up 1.01 percent to 6,000 pesos on turnover of 518.25 million pesos, and cement manufacturer Cementos Caribe, up 2.38 percent to 4,300 pesos per share on volume of 43.4 million pesos.

Banco de Colombia shares edged up 0.23 percent to 432 and shares in insurance company Compania Suramericana de Seguros, part of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial conglomerate, remained unchanged at 18,500.
The trend at this time of year is for investors to consolidate their share holdings ahead of the corporate general assembly season next spring, the broker said.

"The tendency of brokers is to become a little more active at this time of year either to establish a position ahead of a company's general assembly or as a way of reinvesting dividends, but there is still limited external demand," the Bogota broker added.
Another Bogota broker said the day's demand for Banco de Bogota, Suramericana de Seguros and Cementos Caribe may be an indication of foreign investor interest.
"I think these funds are looking for well traded shares and especially preferential shares when companies have issued those in small volumes," he added.

Suramericana de Seguros was active in Medellin, but its shares ended unchanged at 18,500 pesos. Cigarette manufacturer Coltabaco closed unchanged at 3,000 pesos per share on the back of trading volume of 104.9 million pesos.
The dip in Medellin's general price index was sparked by profit-taking in supermarket chain Supermercados Exito, which fell 1.75 percent to 2,800 pesos on turnover of 42 million pesos.
